sections.text:
Company: Neochem Bio Solutions Limited. NSE SME/Emerge symbol: NEOCHEM. ISIN: INE21UM01018. CIN: L24304GJ2017PLC097754. The business incorporated in 2017, adopted its present name in 2025 and listed on 9 December 2025. No current subsidiary, associate or joint venture is reported.
Information cutoff: 20 October 2026. Price reference: 19 October 2026. Documents retrieved: 22 October. Valuation runs from 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031, exactly 1826/365.25 years. Figures are INR crore unless labeled otherwise. The nominal pretax equity-return hurdle is 15%, with 12% and 18% sensitivities. The ₹500,000 liquidity example is illustrative, not the user's portfolio.
The full FY26 annual report, statutory audit, CARO, IFC, audit-trail findings and notes were inspected, together with the final prospectus, restated financials, IPO monitoring and management call. Four fiscal years are authenticated, not five. FY23 includes 98.88%-owned Altius, transferred to promoters in January 2024; the prospectus describes FY24 onward as standalone. Original earlier audit annexures and FY22 full accounts were not authenticated. No H1 FY27 financials were available at cutoff; the September presentation repeats FY26 figures.
Historical evidence has medium-to-high confidence. Current funding and full liquidity evidence have low confidence. Overall investment confidence is therefore low, not an average that hides the critical gaps.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
All 13 factor audits contain supporting facts, contrary facts, judgment and source IDs. Scores are GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 5, CASH 2, BAL 4, EXEC 5, EARN 5, R NS, D 3, P 4 and L NS. REV's mechanical >30% growth band is 9, capped at 8 for limited history and medium confidence.
BQS = 0.80 + 1.00 + 0.96 + 0.60 + 0.60 + 0.20 + 0.32 + 0.40 = 4.88, displayed 4.9. GQS = 3.20 + 1.20 + 0.75 + 0.75 + 0.20 = 6.10 raw, capped at 5.00 because CASH is 2 and aggregate cash conversion is persistently weak.
IAS uses the unrounded 4.88 BQS as Q. Known contribution is 1.22 + 0.60 + 0.40 = 2.22; coverage is 55%, missing weight 45%. The diagnostic range 2.67–6.72 is not a score, confidence interval or permission to rank. R and L are neither imputed at 5 nor reweighted away.
One-point judgment sensitivities are embedded. None removes the evidence needed to clear the funding or tradeability gates. BQS/GQS remain eligible for descriptive quality comparison, with the cash ceiling visible. IAS and investable rankings are excluded.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Neochem formulates specialty performance chemicals across polymers, surfactants, silicones and bio-based esters. Applications include textiles, cleaning, home and personal care, water treatment, coatings, paper and related industries. Its economics are manufacturing and formulation sales, not software licensing or a financial spread. Management describes more than 350 formulations, 50 distributors and 225 domestic customers; these counts are not independently tested retention cohorts.
The single Moraiya plant near Ahmedabad occupies 6,763 square metres, with 22,000 MTPA capacity, 1,350 MT storage and flexible batch production. FY26 output of 11,589 MT represents 52.7% utilization. Spare installed capacity creates real near-term headroom, but does not guarantee demand, cash conversion or permanently zero capital expenditure.
Application knowledge, customization, local service and consistent quality are the customer proposition. Revenue divided by production was approximately ₹95,521 per MT in FY26 versus ₹91,492 in FY25. The implied 4.4% increase is a realization/mix proxy, not an audited invoiced-price or contribution-margin measure: production and sales volumes differ through inventory movements. Customer-level retention, gross contribution and cash payback are not disclosed sufficiently to claim precise unit economics.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Technical qualification and service relationships create moderate switching friction, but a broad durable moat is not established. Consistent formulations, small-batch responsiveness and application assistance can support repeat demand. ISO, ZDHC and GOTS certifications support market access; they are not exclusive rights. Trademarks and the Lamoral fluorine-free collaboration do not establish proprietary patents, exclusive distribution or royalty economics.
Competition is concrete. Rossari's FY26 consolidated revenue was ₹2,396.4 crore, with approximately ₹285.9 crore operating EBITDA excluding other income. Fineotex directly overlaps textile auxiliaries and reported ₹772.2 crore consolidated sales; acquisitions and non-controlling interests materially affect comparability. Fineotex's FY26 CFO was negative too, so larger size does not automatically mean superior cash quality. Galaxy provides a historical FY25 comparator in home/personal-care surfactants and green-chemistry innovation, not a current valuation benchmark.
Most customer sales are short-term orders, and distributors lack long-term exclusive arrangements. The prospectus itself describes fragmented price competition. H1 FY26 top-customer concentration was 24.28% and top-ten concentration 55.09%. These figures look through the related reseller to end customers; they do not measure receivable-counterparty diversification. Proof of a stronger moat would require resilient gross profit per unit, customer retention and collections through a textile downturn.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Revenue was ₹48.1884 crore in FY23, ₹61.1463 crore in FY24, ₹84.1727 crore in FY25 and ₹110.6994 crore in FY26. Three-year reported CAGR is 31.95%; goods-only CAGR is 34.29%; FY24–26 standalone CAGR is 34.55%. FY23 and FY24 included service revenue of ₹2.4829 crore and ₹1.0017 crore respectively, absent thereafter. The FY23 consolidation change limits a strict like-for-like claim. No current acquisition explains the FY25–26 expansion.
Production rose 5,414 → 7,694 → 9,200 → 11,589 MT. This supports real physical scale, not a sales-only narrative. FY26 growth decomposes approximately into 25.97% production growth and 4.40% realization/mix, with the production-versus-sales caveat. Installed capacity remained 22,000 MT, so recent growth mainly uses existing assets.
Textiles declined from 95.92% of goods revenue in FY23 to 85.24% in FY25 and 77.03% in H1 FY26. Management presents home/personal care at 14% in FY26. Audited exports were ₹4.026 crore, just 3.64% of FY26 revenue versus 8.60% in FY25. This is weaker than loose approximately 5% commentary and far below longer-term export ambitions of 30–35%. FY27 utilization near 65% is an aspiration, not authenticated orders. The IPO-commissioned industry report supplies context, not independent proof of future market share.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Growth quality trails growth speed. Operating EBIT excluding all other income rose from ₹3.0115 crore in FY23 to ₹4.7705 crore in FY24, ₹11.4751 crore in FY25 and ₹18.6075 crore in FY26 before exceptional gratuity. At a normalized 25% tax rate, FY24–26 incremental NOPAT was ₹10.3778 crore against ₹45.2332 crore additional broad funded capital: 22.94%. FY26 closing NOPAT/funded capital was only 15.47%, less flattering than plant-only or average-capital ratios after the IPO.
The independent asset-note bridge includes PPE, intangibles, CWIP, inventory, receivables, advances and other assets, less separately transcribed trade, accrual, tax and provision balances. Restricted deposits, subsidy and property rights remain funded capital, not free cash. Only two comparable standalone intervals are available, so durable full-cycle excess returns are not proved. Private project cohorts are not required to assess the available aggregate bridge.
The forward model uses 18% base growth, 17% operating EBIT margin and core operating working capital at 55% of annual sales. Core opening WC explicitly reconciles to ₹66.1577 crore. WC ramps smoothly through each fiscal year rather than prefunding an entire annual increase in April. Maintenance is 1.8% of sales; additional capacity expenditure begins above 1.8 times FY26 sales. Old taxes, statutory dues, gratuity, collateral and a phased cash reserve are explicit. Repayment of all ₹0.834 crore non-WC debt within one year, including related-party debt, is a conservative accelerated-repayment assumption, not a statement that it is all contractually due.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoter-family control, the related reseller and former Altius subsidiary create credit and alignment questions. FY26 related receivables were ₹20.3257 crore, 41.72% of total versus 73.16% in FY25. Their ₹1.8322 crore increase explains only 7.81% of the overall receivables increase. Blaming all deterioration on related parties would be wrong. Reported related sales include GST and cannot be divided directly by net revenue without qualification.
Director remuneration of ₹1.2888 crore was about 10.7% of PAT; related rents were ₹0.51 crore. Directors advanced ₹6.18 crore and recovered ₹7.7519 crore during FY26. Separately, ₹6.25 crore was allocated to unquoted Punit Fintrade, Aryaman Enterprise and Alfa Fiscal investments. No liquid redemption terms were retrieved. This deserves scrutiny alongside credit-funded growth, but is not proof of illegality or diversion.
Production and operating leverage improved. Collection execution did not match the prospectus's 100-day FY26 closing-receivables plan: the actual closing measure was 160.7 days. The approximately 122-day average-balance measure is a different denominator, not achievement of the closing target. Management said more than 35% of year-end receivables, over ₹17.05 crore, were collected by May and expected normalization by FY27 end. That is meaningful counterevidence to assuming no collection, but not an audited October cash balance or proof that all old receivables recovered.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Read the notes, not only the headline opinion. FY26 has an unmodified audit, positive IFC/audit-trail findings, and no identified default, wilful default or fraud in CARO. Notes 2.12/2.13 nonetheless disclose bank-stock-statement differences: debtors ₹63.36 lakh and creditors ₹7.88 lakh, approximately 1.30% and 0.68% of the respective balances. The auditor obtained management explanations and found them satisfactory. The precise cause is not printed; neither “no differences” nor “unexplained fraud” is supported.
Emphasis covers ₹4.854 crore SGST subsidy receivable, including ₹2.484 crore FY26 income, and ₹0.2797 crore due from insolvent Morarjee Textiles. The latter is only 0.35% of equity. Neochem’s oral-approval/pending-order wording is superseded by the 11 May 2026 NCLT written order, publicly confirmed on 12 May. The July 2025 register admits ₹31.98637 lakh under its former legal name, versus the different audited ₹27.97 lakh carrying amount; no unexplained reconciliation is invented. The order allocates ₹10 lakh to other operational creditors against ₹38.2683 crore admitted, only about 0.2613% in aggregate. This is not an authenticated Neochem recovery rate or receipt. The 60-day payment provision and wider T+360 implementation schedule are obligations, not proof of completion. Written approval and admission are positive progress but weak support for full realization. Neither item is cash. All other income is excluded from operating valuation, and core scenarios assume no subsidy recovery. Note 34 also reports ₹7.34 lakh disputed tax despite generic CARO language; historical delayed dues are retained separately from present no-default findings.
FY26 pre-WC operating cash was ₹21.8450 crore. Receivables consumed ₹23.4466 crore, inventory ₹5.4984 crore, supplier paydown ₹5.1680 crore and cash taxes ₹2.9622 crore, with other movements producing CFO of −₹16.9378 crore. Interest of ₹3.5052 crore is financing-classified, giving post-interest CFO of −₹20.4430 crore. Capital expenditure does not explain this weak CFO.
A ₹2.6794 crore capital advance disappeared while land additions were ₹2.7437 crore. The ₹2.1247 crore other-NCA release reconciles to this advance less FD and security-deposit additions. A neutral transfer diagnostic adjusts CFO to −₹19.6172 crore and gross cash capex to ₹0.2750 crore; after-capex cash is unchanged. It is not an additional cash loss. FY25 PAT/gratuity timing and equal-and-opposite CFO/CFI reclassifications are likewise preserved without asserting fraud. Prior EPS ₹11.15 was not bonus-adjusted; ₹6.3694 uses the corrected denominator. Full financial, ageing and reconciliation rows are embedded.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The exchange-authenticated ₹106.90 price and 17,120,753 shares imply ₹183.0208 crore market capitalization. Adding March gross debt of ₹17.7935 crore and deducting only ₹0.181 crore free cash produces mechanical EV of ₹200.6333 crore. This is 10.11 times normalized operating EBITDA, 15.22 times reported PAT, or 16.16 times normalized after-interest profit at 25% tax. It is explicitly an October-price/March-balance-sheet calculation, not verified current EV. Restricted deposits, unquoted investments, subsidy and property rights are not treated as cash or counted again at exit.
The funded base uses 18% growth, 17% operating EBIT margin, 55% WC and 12 times exit EBIT. Its 25.17% conditional CAGR and ₹163.3 15%-hurdle entry price are scenario outputs, not buy targets. Corresponding 12%/18% hurdle prices are ₹186.4/₹143.6. Bear growth/margin/collection assumptions breach before entry and produce no non-rescue return. The bullish 44.3% scenario requires faster growth, better cash conversion and a 16-times multiple.
The independent FCFF anchor uses a separately reasoned WACC range of 12%/14%/16%, not the equity hurdle by identity. Central 14% approximates 90% equity at 14.8% required return and 10% debt at 6.75% after-tax cost. This is an analyst capital-cost assumption, not a measured CAPM estimate. Terminal growth is 4%, incremental terminal ROIC 18%, with a 2%/4%/5% terminal-growth grid. Full ₹1 crore operating cash is reserved at entry, conservatively covering future reserve build. Base central DCF is ₹85.4; bull is ₹128.6. The discrepancy with 12-times exit EBIT is substantive and should not be averaged away.
Finite funded reverse-expectation brackets are checked. The exit-multiple method needs about 7.13% growth for a 15% return under its other assumptions. The central-DCF scan has no funded crossing at the market price: its last funded grid point, 21% growth, values equity at about ₹90.6 per share; 22% and higher fail the funding test under the same base assumptions. That endpoint is not called a required-growth solution. All ordinary returns and buy prices remain NS. Complete monthly, annual, growth/multiple, WC/margin, capex/WC/headroom and WACC/terminal-growth rows are embedded.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The linked permanent-loss path is customer weakness → lower utilization and margin → slower collections and inventory buildup → constrained drawing power/collateral → expensive financing or dilution. IPO equity reduces leverage but cannot make debtors immediately spendable. The bear path fails before entry, so no ordinary five-year return is shown as if the company could survive it automatically.
For illustration, haircuts of 10% to receivables and inventory, plus full nonrealization of subsidy, unquoted investments and property rights, reduce ₹78.8447 crore book equity to about ₹56.24 crore, or ₹32.85 per share. This is neither fair value nor a liquidation floor. Taxes, recovery costs and other realizable assets may differ. The small individual Morarjee exposure is not exaggerated into the whole downside thesis.
An explicitly hypothetical rescue triples capex under base operating assumptions. That reference path survives through entry but fails later. A fictional 19 October issue at ₹85.5, a 20% discount, with 3% fees requires 5,810,900 whole new shares. Gross proceeds of ₹49.7 crore less ₹1.5 crore fees yield ₹48.2 crore to prefund future uses. Existing-holder ownership dilution is 25.3%, distinct from 33.9% share expansion. This is not announced or available financing. The failed unrescued return stays suppressed; any rescued return has its own label. Entry-date rescue cannot cure a pre-entry failure.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Both 5× and 10× are speculative/unsupported, not declared impossible. From ₹106.90, the required equity values are approximately ₹915.1 crore and ₹1,830.2 crore. At 12 times EBIT and a 17% operating margin, ignoring net-debt contribution, necessary revenue is roughly ₹448.6 crore and ₹897.2 crore. At constant FY26 realization this means approximately 47,000 and 94,000 MT, far beyond the 22,000 MT plant.
The six embedded rows cross 5×/10× with 8/12/16 times exit EBIT, solve necessary revenue and growth, show implied physical capacity and rerun funding. These are necessary conditions, not promised outcomes: terminal debt, cash and dilution can prevent the equity goal even when operating targets are met. A funding-failed scenario has no displayed non-rescue return, and an off-domain solver endpoint is not called a required solution.
A supported 5× case would need several times current sales, financed capacity, credible customer demand, better cash realization and valuation support. A 10× case demands materially more. There is no defensible precise success probability. Repeated collection-backed growth, nonsubsidy earnings, durable incremental returns after working capital and appropriately financed expansion could improve the assessment. Higher reported PAT or an aspirational export target alone would not.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Next financial release: reconcile year-end receivables by ageing/counterparty to subsequent cash, credit notes, write-offs and new invoices. Identify how much of the May collection claim came from old or related balances. Track both closing and average DSO, six-/twelve-month ageing, inventory, supplier terms and post-interest CFO. Repeatable conversion is stronger evidence than one quarter's EPS.
Funding: updated borrowings, cash, facility limits and renewal, eligible drawing power, and actual RD/FD encumbrances. Reconcile legacy taxes, statutory dues and gratuity. Do not reuse fully spent IPO proceeds or add headline credit limits without collateral conditions. Clarify the liquidity and economic purpose of the unquoted investments and related credit.
Operations: production, realized mix, utilization against the approximately 65% FY27 ambition, nontextile demand, exports against the audited 3.64% starting share, maintenance and expansion spending. Audit/governance: subsidy eligibility and cash recovery, Morarjee's individual settlement terms and actual receipts under the approved plan, changed audit findings, bank-return explanations and comparative EPS/PAT clarification.
Market: complete actual 20-/60-session issuer observations, dated SME restrictions, spread/depth and whole-lot capacity. Sufficient published evidence can clear funding; private daily statements are not the sole test. Tradeability must be assessed for the stated position rather than inferred from market-maker obligations. This report does not create a recurring monitoring service or authorize any trade.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved; mixed-quality, high-growth research watchlist. BQS 4.88 belongs in the 4–<6 quality band. Raw GQS 6.10 is capped at 5.00 for cash weakness. IAS remains NS, so no investment-setup score is invented. Funding and tradeability Holds exclude investable rankings; descriptive BQS/GQS comparison can retain the disclosed flags.
No quality-compounder designation is justified yet. Strong volume growth does not settle cash conversion, minority-capital allocation or sustainable reinvestment quality. The appropriate conditional action is to wait for collection and funding verification, not to use the ₹163 exit-multiple-derived hurdle price as a buy instruction. The independently reasoned central DCF of about ₹85.4, below the ₹106.90 price, illustrates the terminal-valuation risk.
If updated published financials demonstrate current financeability and aged-debtor recovery without damaging dilution, rerun all cash, valuation and tradeability tests. If collections continue deteriorating or material audit/funding concerns emerge, reassess the gates before extrapolating growth. This analysis does not assert observed default, proven fraud, guaranteed execution or suitability for a particular investor.

sections.text:
The source register links full primary documents, their relevant pages and authenticated payload hashes where available. It includes the FY26 annual report, final prospectus, December/March IPO monitoring, May call, September presentation, NSE quote/security master three peer sources, and the Morarjee tribunal order, exchange confirmation and sanitized old-name creditor admission.
